OpenAI is filing for an IPO — and for the first time, the AI industry's real economics will be public record.

This is not just a funding milestone. The S-1 filing will disclose exactly how OpenAI's revenue breaks down between ChatGPT subscriptions, developer API access, and enterprise contracts. More critically, it will reveal unit economics: whether the company makes or loses money on every user and every query at scale.

For business leaders, this changes the game. Those numbers will become the benchmark against which every AI vendor, every AI budget line, and every build-versus-buy decision gets measured. If OpenAI shows sustainable margins, it validates the enterprise AI spending wave. If it reveals structural losses, it means the AI pricing environment many companies depend on today is artificially subsidized — and likely to shift.

Either outcome demands that executive teams stress-test their current AI strategies against what these disclosures might reveal. The leaders who scenario-plan now will be positioned to act decisively when the numbers drop.
